nodes.summary: For every stack $S$ and every finite sequence $\sigma$ of stack operations, if running $\sigma$ on $S$ succeeds with final stack $F$, then the cost of the run plus the number of elements of $F$ equals the number of elements of $S$ plus twice the number of PUSH operations in $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Cost balance for stack operation sequences

nodes.summary: For every stack $S$ and every finite sequence $\sigma$ of stack operations, running POP followed by $\sigma$ on $S$ has the same result and cost as first performing the standalone POP on $S$ and then, if it reports underflow, stopping with an error at no further cost, or, if it removes the top element and leaves the stack $S'$, running $\sigma$ on $S'$, the two costs being added.
nodes.title: Running a POP agrees with the standalone POP

nodes.summary: For every stack $S$, every value $x$ and every finite sequence $\sigma$ of stack operations, running PUSH $x$ followed by $\sigma$ on $S$ has the same result and cost as first performing the standalone PUSH of $x$ on $S$ and then running $\sigma$ on the resulting stack, the two costs being added.
nodes.title: Running a PUSH agrees with the standalone PUSH

nodes.summary: For every stack $S$ and every sequence of $n$ stack operations (PUSH, POP and MULTIPOP), if running the sequence on $S$ succeeds, that is, no POP meets an empty stack, then its cost is at most $|S| + 2n$, where $|S|$ is the number of elements of $S$.
nodes.title: Aggregate cost of stack operation sequences

nodes.summary: Given a stack $S$ and a finite sequence of operations, each a PUSH of a value, a POP or a MULTIPOP with an integer count, the operations are applied to $S$ in order. PUSH of $x$ puts $x$ on top at cost $1$; POP removes the top element at cost $1$; MULTIPOP with count $k$ is MULTIPOP with an integer count, costing one unit per element removed. If a POP meets an empty stack, the run stops and reports an error, that…
nodes.title: Running a sequence of stack operations

nodes.summary: For every stack $S$, stored as a list with its top first, and every natural number $k$, the stack returned by MULTIPOP of $S$ with count $k$ is $S$ with its top $k$ elements removed, or the empty stack if $S$ has fewer than $k$ elements.
nodes.title: Result of MULTIPOP

nodes.summary: For every stack $S$ and every integer $k \le 0$, MULTIPOP with integer count $k$ applied to $S$ returns $S$ at cost $0$.
nodes.title: MULTIPOP with a nonpositive count does nothing

nodes.summary: For a stack $S$ and an integer $k$, MULTIPOP with integer count $k$ is MULTIPOP of $S$ with the natural count $\max(k, 0)$, with the same result and cost. In particular, a count $k \le 0$ removes nothing.
nodes.title: MULTIPOP with an integer count

nodes.summary: For every stack $S$ and every natural number $k$, the cost of MULTIPOP of $S$ with count $k$ is $\min(|S|, k)$, where $|S|$ is the number of elements of $S$.
nodes.title: Cost of MULTIPOP

nodes.summary: For a stack $S$, stored as a list with its top first, and a natural number $k$, MULTIPOP of $S$ with count $k$ repeatedly removes the top element while the stack is nonempty and fewer than $k$ elements have been removed, and returns the remaining stack. Each removed element costs one unit, and nothing else is charged.
nodes.title: MULTIPOP

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of stack entries, a stack operation is one of the following: $\mathrm{PUSH}(x)$ for an element $x \in \alpha$, $\mathrm{POP}$, or $\mathrm{MULTIPOP}(k)$ for an integer count $k$.
nodes.title: Stack operations for the MULTIPOP aggregate analysis

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $s$ be a stack over $\alpha$ (a list of elements of $\alpha$ whose first element is the top) and let $v \in \alpha$. Pushing $v$ onto $s$ returns the stack with top $v$ followed by the elements of $s$, at cost $1$. Popping $s$ returns underflow (no value) at cost $0$ if $s$ is empty, and returns the pair $(h, t)$ at cost $1$ if $s$ has top $h$ and remaining stack $t$. Reading the top of…
nodes.title: Result and cost of the stack operations

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a stack over a type $\alpha$ (a list of elements of $\alpha$ whose first element is the top). If $s$ is empty, popping $s$ returns underflow (no value) at cost $0$. If $s$ has top $h$ and remaining stack $t$, popping $s$ returns the pair $(h, t)$ at cost $1$.
nodes.title: Result and cost of stack pop

nodes.summary: Stacks over a type $\alpha$ are lists of elements of $\alpha$, with the first element as the top. Popping the empty stack returns underflow (no value) at cost $0$. Popping a stack with top $v$ and remaining stack $t$ returns the pair $(v, t)$ at cost $1$ (one successful pop event).
nodes.title: Stack pop

nodes.summary: Stacks over a type $\alpha$ are lists of elements of $\alpha$, with the first element as the top. Pushing $v \in \alpha$ onto a stack $s$ returns the stack with top $v$ followed by the elements of $s$, at cost $1$ (one successful push event).
nodes.title: Stack push

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a stack over a type $\alpha$ (a list of elements of $\alpha$ whose first element is the top). If $s$ is empty, reading the top of $s$ returns underflow (no value) at cost $0$. If $s$ has top $h$, reading the top of $s$ returns $h$ at cost $1$.
nodes.title: Result and cost of reading the stack top

nodes.summary: Stacks over a type $\alpha$ are lists of elements of $\alpha$, with the first element as the top. Reading the top of the empty stack returns underflow (no value) at cost $0$. Reading the top of a stack with top $v$ returns $v$ at cost $1$ (one successful top event); the stack itself is not returned or changed.
nodes.title: Stack top

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
